title: ReelDesi
pitch: You are building a short video app for people who speak Bhojpuri, Marathi and other Indian languages, where small creators can be seen and earn. You have ₹2 crore from angel investors. In about two years you must reach 50,000 monthly users, earn as much as you spend each month from ads, and keep users' trust.

stages.title: Find the real problem
stages.situation: You want to build a short video app for people who speak Bhojpuri, Marathi and other Indian languages. You have one month to learn what's missing in the apps they use today.

options.label: Run a poll on your Instagram page
options.outcome: Most say they want 'more filters' and 'celebrity videos'.
options.lesson: Your followers are not your users. Polls tell you wishes, not real needs.

later.note: Users who joined for filters got bored fast. Filters were never the real reason to stay.

options.label: Spend 3 weeks with 30 small creators in Bihar and Maharashtra
options.detail: See how they make and share videos.
options.outcome: The real pain: their videos get lost on big apps, and they can't earn anything even with 10,000 followers.
options.lesson: Watching creators shows the real problem: being seen and earning, not editing tools.

options.label: Copy the biggest short video app
options.outcome: You save time, but creators have no reason to move.
options.lesson: A copy has to be better somewhere, or nobody switches.

stages.title: Pick your first users
stages.situation: Who do you build for first?

options.label: Bhojpuri creators and their fans
options.detail: One language, a hungry audience, ignored by big apps.
options.outcome: Creators bring their fans. Fans find more creators in their language.
options.lesson: A community the big players ignore can become your stronghold.

options.label: Everyone in India, all languages
options.outcome: Feeds feel random. No language community forms.
options.lesson: A social app needs density. Spread too thin and nobody finds their people.

options.label: English speaking college students in big cities
options.outcome: They join, then go back to Instagram where their friends are.
options.lesson: Users who already have a home on a giant app rarely move.

later.note: Instagram launched a new feature, and your city students went back.

stages.title: Build the first version
stages.situation: You have two months to launch.

options.label: Simple video posting with a feed that shows new creators to fans in their language
options.outcome: New creators get their first 500 views in a day. They post more.
options.lesson: In a creator app, helping creators get seen is the core job.

options.label: Full studio: editing, effects, music, live streaming, chat
options.outcome: It's heavy and slow on cheap phones. Half your users can't open it.
options.lesson: More features don't win if the basics don't work on your users' phones.

options.label: No content moderation, to grow faster
options.outcome: Content explodes. So does harmful content.
options.lesson: Skipping safety in a social app invites trouble from users, brands and the law.

later.note: Hateful and adult videos spread on your app. The app store warned you and brands pulled out.

stages.title: How will you make money?
stages.situation: Users won't pay for a video app. How do you earn?

options.label: Short ads between videos, and share ad money with top creators
options.outcome: Creators push their fans to the app because they earn from it.
options.lesson: Sharing money with creators makes them your best marketers.

options.label: Pay ₹10 to every new user for signing up
options.outcome: Sign ups explode. Many are fake accounts made for the money.
options.lesson: Paying for sign ups attracts people who want money, not your product.

later.note: You stopped the sign up bonus. Most of those accounts went silent.

options.label: ₹49 a month to remove ads
options.outcome: Few users pay. Many feel the free app is now spammed with ads.
options.lesson: Charging before users love the product slows growth.

stages.title: Launch
stages.situation: How do you get your first big wave of users?

options.label: Sign up 200 local creators who bring their fans
options.outcome: Each creator brings a few hundred loyal fans.
options.lesson: In social apps, creators bring the audience.

options.label: ₹30 lakh on ads
options.outcome: Installs jump, but people find an empty feed with few creators.
options.lesson: Users without content to watch leave fast.

later.note: Most users from the ads found nothing they liked and left.

options.label: Referral: ₹20 for both friends
options.outcome: Friends join together. Some fake accounts too.
options.lesson: Referrals work, but guard against fraud.

stages.title: First week experience
stages.situation: New users scroll for a minute and leave. What do you fix?

options.label: Ask for their language and 3 favourite topics, then show the best videos first
options.detail: A good feed from minute one.
options.outcome: New users find something they love in the first minute.
options.lesson: The first session must show the product's best. A good first feed is activation for a video app.

options.label: Send 5 notifications a day
options.outcome: People turn off notifications or delete the app.
options.lesson: Notifications can't fix a boring feed.

options.label: Coins for watching videos
options.outcome: Watch time goes up. Many leave the app running for coins.
options.lesson: Rewards can create fake engagement.

stages.title: Choose your north star
stages.situation: The team needs one number to chase every week.

options.label: Users who watch and creators who post at least 3 days a week
options.outcome: Teams work on creator growth and feed quality together.
options.lesson: A social app needs both sides healthy. The north star should capture both.

options.label: App downloads
options.outcome: Marketing wins, the product suffers.
options.lesson: Downloads don't show value.

options.label: Total minutes watched
options.outcome: The feed starts pushing shocking clickbait to keep people watching.
options.lesson: Chasing only watch time can make a feed worse for users and for trust.

stages.title: Grow the team
stages.situation: You have 15,000 users. Who do you hire?

options.label: A trust and safety lead and a creator partnerships team
options.outcome: Harmful content drops. Creators feel supported.
options.lesson: In social apps, safety and creator care are core.

options.label: 10 junior developers to add features
options.outcome: Features pile up. Nobody watches what's being posted.
options.lesson: Features don't replace the work of looking after a community.

later.note: A rushed update broke video uploads on cheap phones for a week.

options.label: Stay lean, founders review content
options.outcome: You save money but the founders watch videos all night.
options.lesson: Burnout is a real cost.

later.note: Tired founders missed harmful videos and creators' messages.

stages.title: Raise money
stages.situation: Investors are interested. How much do you raise?

options.label: ₹10 crore, promise 12 languages in a year
options.outcome: Huge cash, huge expectations.
options.lesson: Growing to new languages before one works copies your problems.

later.note: You launched 10 languages with too few creators each. Costs exploded.

options.label: ₹3 crore from founders of social and media apps
options.outcome: Enough runway, and investors who know creator economies.
options.lesson: Smart money brings advice, not just cash.

options.label: Don't raise. Aim for profit.
options.outcome: You stay careful, but growth slows.
options.lesson: Social apps usually need scale before they earn well, so be careful.

stages.title: Build a growth engine
stages.situation: You want growth that keeps going on its own. What do you build?

options.label: One-tap sharing to WhatsApp with your watermark and a link back
options.outcome: Videos spread through family groups. Viewers install to see more.
options.lesson: When content travels with your name on it, growth runs itself. TikTok grew this way.

options.label: TV ads during a cricket match
options.outcome: A spike, mostly people who don't speak your languages.
options.lesson: Expensive reach to the wrong people doesn't last.

later.note: Most TV sign ups found no videos in their language and left.

options.label: Add 4 more languages
options.outcome: Users grow, but each language needs its own creators and moderators.
options.lesson: New markets bring growth and new costs.

stages.title: Earn more per user
stages.situation: You need more money per user. What do you try?

options.label: More ads between videos
options.outcome: Money rises. Some users complain.
options.lesson: Ads can work if they don't ruin the experience.

options.label: Charge creators to boost their videos
options.outcome: Small creators feel the feed is now for those who pay.
options.lesson: Making creators pay to be seen breaks your core promise.

options.label: Brand deals: connect local brands with creators and take a small cut
options.detail: Creators earn more, you earn too.
options.outcome: Slow start. Then local brands line up.
options.lesson: Helping your users earn, and taking a share, builds strong margins.

later.note: Local brands love your creators. Brand deal income is growing fast.

stages.title: A giant enters
stages.situation: A big social app launches a Bhojpuri section and pays creators to move.

options.label: Pay creators even more to stay
options.outcome: Creators stay, but you are burning cash fast.
options.lesson: Bidding wars favour the player with the most money.

later.note: The bidding war ended. Your cash is gone, and some creators left anyway.

options.label: Ignore money. Double down on helping creators grow and earn from brands
options.outcome: Some creators try the giant. Their videos get lost there.
options.lesson: Compete on what makes you different.

later.note: Creators came back. 'There, I'm one of millions. Here, my fans see me,' one said.

options.label: Pivot to a video editing tool
options.outcome: Users feel dropped. The team is confused.
options.lesson: Running from competition throws away what you built.

stages.title: A crisis
stages.situation: A fake video about a riot spreads on your app and causes panic in a town.

options.label: Remove it fast, show a fact check, work with police, add a fake news team
options.detail: Act fast and fix the system.
options.outcome: It costs money, but people and the government see you act responsibly.
options.lesson: Social apps carry responsibility for what spreads. Act fast and openly.

options.label: Say you're just a platform, not responsible
options.outcome: The government and press turn on you.
options.lesson: Avoiding responsibility makes a crisis much worse.

options.label: Blame the user who posted it
options.outcome: People ask why it spread so far on your app.
options.lesson: Users hold you responsible for what your feed promotes.

stages.title: Top creators want a better deal
stages.situation: Your top 100 creators say their share of ad money is too small.

options.label: Raise their share and give them early access to features
options.outcome: Costs rise, but creators post more and promote you.
options.lesson: In a creator app, creators are your supply. Keep them happy.

options.label: Ignore them, there are always new creators
options.outcome: Top creators leave and take their fans.
options.lesson: Losing your best supply hurts more than it saves.

options.label: Pay more to creators whose fans stay longest
options.outcome: Great creators earn more. Some feel the rules are unclear.
options.lesson: Paying for outcomes can work if rules are clear.

stages.title: The road to profit
stages.situation: Investors want a clear path to profit before the next round.

options.label: Shut down the 3 languages with the fewest users
options.outcome: Some users leave, but costs fall a lot.
options.lesson: Cutting losing parts focuses the business on what works.

options.label: Launch in Indonesia now
options.outcome: Big new costs before the core is profitable.
options.lesson: Expanding to escape problems usually multiplies them.

options.label: Show 5% more ads
options.outcome: A bit more money. Some users leave.
options.lesson: Small changes add up, but watch trust and growth.

events.title: A video goes hugely viral
events.situation: A creator's song on your app is everywhere. Millions want to watch.

options.label: Add servers fast and feature similar creators
options.outcome: New users stay for more creators.
options.lesson: Prepare to catch a wave when it comes.

options.label: Do nothing special
options.outcome: The app slows down and new users leave.
options.lesson: Missing your big moment is costly.

events.title: Uploads fail
events.situation: Your video storage provider has an outage.

options.label: Save uploads on the phone and post them later, tell creators
options.outcome: Creators lose nothing.
options.lesson: Have a backup plan for your key tools.

options.label: Wait for it to come back
options.outcome: Creators lose videos and get angry.
options.lesson: Users don't care whose fault it is.

events.title: A rival poaches your head of creators
events.situation: Your head of creator partnerships has a big offer.

options.label: Counter-offer with equity
options.outcome: They stay.
options.lesson: Key people are worth investing in.

options.label: Let them go and promote from within
options.outcome: A few big creators leave with them.
options.lesson: Losing key people has a cost.

events.title: New rules for social apps
events.situation: The government says social apps must remove fake news within 24 hours and name a grievance officer.

options.label: Follow them right away and say so
options.outcome: Some extra cost, but you look responsible.
options.lesson: Following rules early builds trust.

options.label: Wait and see
options.outcome: You get a legal notice and bad press.
options.lesson: Rules for user safety are a floor, not an option.
